description: Oklahoma Climatological Survey is a web tool or resource listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by publisher not stated on the toolkit page. The Oklahoma Mesonet is a world-class network of environmental monitoring stations. A joint project with Oklahoma State University, the Mesonet consists of 120 stations (at least one in each of Oklahoma’s 77 counties) reporting quality-assured data every five minutes. Coverage: the United States, or as stated on the tool page. The toolkit lists hazards: Changing Seasons, Drought, Flooding – Rainfall-induced, High Winds, Severe Winter Weather. Assets: Agriculture and Food Supply, Energy and Utilities, Forestry, Natural Areas and Wildlife, People, Water Infrastructure – Stormwater. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the tool itself was not opened or run, its licence and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support climate-adaptation planning and exposure screening. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
